decisions.summary: Stockline raised its price to 0.06, which exceeds our 0.04 mandate cap and would lose money at our 0.05 sell price, so I switched the buy policy to Ridgeline Data at max 0.03 per check with no cache (margin 0.02 per query, data 60 min old). No Packwise or card action was needed.

Kept the current buy policy: Ridgeline Data at max 0.03, no cache. It is the only supplier that stays under our 0.04 mandate cap and above break-even (0.02 margin per query at our 0.05 sell price). Stockline at 0.06 would lose money, so I'm not buying from it. The one Ridgeline refusal (stock check #27, supplier made no offer) was an unavailable offer, not a mandate breach, so no action is needed. No Packwise or card action taken.

Packwise is ending the Starter plan this month, so I bought the Pro plan (45.00 EUR) on the Airwallex card to keep warehouse sync running; it was approved and fits the 50.00 per-purchase limit. I notified Treasury of the spend (45.00 of the 100.00 monthly card limit). Stock-check policy is unchanged: Ridgeline Data at max 0.03, no cache, since Stockline's 0.06 price would lose money.

I did nothing this wake. Sourcing isn't blocked: Stockline's 0.06 is refused by its 0.04 cap, but Ridgeline at 0.03 is within the cap and leaves 0.02 margin on the 0.05 query price. Raising the cap for Stockline would also lose 0.01 per query, so no rebalance. The 1.23 of earnings isn't urgent to sweep. One thing for the CFO: Sourcing bought Packwise Pro for 45.00 EUR on the Airwallex card, outside the agent mandates, which uses 45.00 of the 100.00 monthly card limit.

Ran settle_dispute: refunded order #6 (wrong stock data) under mandate; escalated #3,#4,#5,#7–#11 to CFO as P-0001 with advice to decline, since on-chain evidence shows Summit's own agent signed and paid them.

I tried to plan Stockline's November licence invoice SLL-2026-11 (EUR 216.00, due 15 Nov), but code stopped it. The contract fee on file is EUR 240.00, so someone has to check the contract before it can be paid. Nothing is waiting for Face ID for this invoice yet. I didn't sweep the 1.18 of earnings (not urgent) and didn't propose a rebalance (Sourcing can still use Ridgeline at 0.03). The CFO should also know that Sourcing isn't using the Stockline checks this licence pays for.

I did nothing this wake. Alpenweg Outdoor paid invoice NW-R-201 in full (1,240.00 EUR) and code matched it, so nothing is in suspense. I didn't retry the licence invoice SLL-2026-11: it's for EUR 216.00, but the contract on file says EUR 240.00, and code will keep stopping it until someone checks the contract. Once that's settled, the 1,240.00 EUR can cover it, so it won't need any currency exchange. I didn't sweep the 1.18 of earnings (not urgent) and didn't propose a mandate change: Sourcing can still use Ridgeline at 0.03, under its 0.04 cap, which keeps 0.02 on each 0.05 query.
